sources.entry: cirq - A Google-developed framework focused on hardware-aware quantum circuit design for NISQ devices.

summary.one_liner: Cirq is a Python package for writing, manipulating, and running quantum circuits on quantum computers and simulators, developed by Google Quantum AI.
summary.what_it_does: Cirq provides abstractions for building and transforming quantum circuits, with a focus on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware where device details matter. According to the README, it supports flexible and custom gate definitions, parameterized circuits with symbolic variables, circuit transformation, compilation and optimization, hardware device modeling, and noise modeling. It includes multiple built-in circuit simulators and integrates with qsim for high-performance simulation. The README also mentions interoperability with NumPy and SciPy. A "Hello Qubit" example builds a single-qubit circuit, prints it, and runs repeated measurements with cirq.Simulator. The README points to related Google projects for specific needs: Qualtran (fault-tolerant algorithms), Stim (large Clifford circuits and error correction), OpenFermion (chemistry), TensorFlow Quantum (machine learning), and ReCirq (experiments).
use_cases: build and simulate quantum circuits in Python
model quantum hardware devices and noise
run parameterized quantum circuits with symbolic variables
notable: Hardware-aware design for NISQ devices, including device modeling and noise modeling
Integrates with qsim for high-performance simulation
Part of a wider Google Quantum AI software suite (Qualtran, Stim, OpenFermion, TensorFlow Quantum, ReCirq)
Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and Google Colab per the README
Official docs, Jupyter tutorials, and video tutorials
caveats: README says it is not an officially supported Google product
Installation details are deferred to the online documentation
